description: The company's inbox, read every five minutes: every mail becomes a ticket on the board, the reply is drafted in the brand's voice and goes out through the gate, as the company's own address
client_copy: Lee la casilla de la empresa, te deja cada mail como tarea en el tablero y la respuesta escrita esperando tu ok.
_comment: READING IS A FLOW AND ANSWERING IS A GATED TOOL, and that split is the
whole plugin. `flows/bandeja-de-entrada/FLOW.md` wakes the agent every five
minutes (the engine's floor, CORE_FLOWS_MIN_MINUTES); its run calls
`fetch_mail()` once and, with nothing new, ends in one line and costs a
cent. Nothing loops, nothing polls inside a turn, and a restart replays
nothing: IMAP's \Seen flag is the state and the `mail_seen` table is the
second lock.
IT REQUIRES kanban BECAUSE A MAIL IS A TICKET. There is no mail store of
our own and no second screen: a message that arrives lands on the board the
client already reads (`source: mail`, `source_ref`: the Message-ID, which
is the UNIQUE index the board dedupes on). And it requires `approval`
because answering is the one thing this plugin does outwards:
`send_email` is registered on the FACE wrapped in `approval_required()`,
so nothing leaves the building without the client's yes.
THE TOOL HAS NO `to` AND NO `subject`. Both come off the ticket's thread
(`mail_threads`), written by the code when the mail came in, so there is no
way for the model to answer somebody who never wrote. It is the same shape
as the social plugin's `publish_instagram`, whose only argument is a post
id.
THE MODULES CARRY THE `mail_` PREFIX ON PURPOSE. A plugin's surface modules
import each other by plain name and share ONE `sys.modules` namespace with
every other enabled plugin's (`engine/core/plugins.py`): a `store.py` here
would BE the approval plugin's `store`, already imported under that name.
Measured twice already, on the social plugin's `routes.py` and on the
board's.
THE CURATED FLOW IS COPIED INTO THE WORKSPACE AT LOAD, if it is not there.
On this engine a flow is a file in `workspace/flows/` and there is no
install step between the kit and the container -- the kit is a read-only
bind mount. So the engine's loader copies every plugin's `surfaces.flows`,
once, and never over a file that exists (engine/core/plugins.py): what the
client edited is hers, and turning it off is `status: paused`, which is
still a file.
